{#sdcr} # Anlotinib enhances the antitumor immunity of radiotherapy by activating cGAS/STING in non-small cell lung cancer

{#qkg1} # Abstract

{#vut4} Radiation resistance and unsatisfactory efficacy of radioimmunotherapy are important barriers to non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) treatment. The impacts of anlotinib on radiation and tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) in NSCLC remain to be resolved. Here, we find anlotinib enhances radiosensitivity, and further increases radiotherapy-stimulated CD8<sup>+</sup> T cell infiltration and activation via triggering cGAS/STING pathway. Moreover, anlotinib shows significant effects on radioimmunotherapy (radiotherapy plus anti-PD-L1). The addition of anlotinib alleviates CD8<sup>+</sup> T cell exhaustion, promotes the cytotoxicity and proliferation of CD8<sup>+</sup> T cells, and boosts immune memory activation. Our work reveals the crucial role of anlotinib in antitumor immunity, and provides preclinical evidence for the application of anlotinib combined with radioimmunotherapy in NSCLC treatment.

ops.markdown: The mechanisms by which RT induces tumor regression are complex and multifactorial. In the current study, we found that cGAS/STING influenced the infiltration, activation and exhaustion of CD8<sup>+</sup> T cells. However, the addition of a STING inhibitor did not significantly affect CD8<sup>+</sup> T cell proliferation, the CD8<sup>+</sup>Ki67<sup>+</sup>/Foxp3<sup>+</sup>Ki67<sup>+</sup> ratio, Foxp3 expression or immune memory activation compared with triple therapy, indicating that DDR-induced cGAS/STING activation was not the sole regulator of these responses. Other mechanisms, such as endoplasmic reticulum stress and metabolic reprogramming [@w:w30], may therefore also contribute to shaping the RT-induced TIME and warrant further investigation in NSCLC.
